newsitem.title: GERMANY: Germany sees stability pact agreement by December.
newsitem.headline: Germany sees stability pact agreement by December.

text.p: Germany said on Monday that it would be possible to agree by December the main points of a so-called stability pact to enforce budget discipline among European states taking part in the launch of a common currency.

Government spokesman Peter Haussmann, rejecting earlier remarks by European Union officials that tough German demands would force a delay until next year, also said that Bonn wanted the pact to be credible and solid.
Haussmann told reporters it would be possible to thrash out a deal in time for a summit of European Union leaders in Dublin on December 13-14.
"With the goodwill of all involved it will be possible to achieve an agreement on the significant elements (of the stability pact) before the European (summit)," Haussmann said.
"The most important goal of the Federal Republic is that the stability pact will be credible and solid," he said.

Germany wants tough penalties against countries which flout the conditions set in the Maastricht treaty, fearing that a breakdown in financial discipline could make the planned euro currency weaker than the stable mark.
